prompt: A teacher's ages: $30, 31, 32, 33, 65$. Which is a better summary of "typical age"?
hint: Four of the ages are in the low thirties, and one age is very different from the rest.

hints.text: Four of the ages are in the low thirties, and one age is very different from the rest.
The age $65$ is an outlier. Work out the mean, $191 \div 5$, and the median, the middle of $30, 31, 32, 33, 65$, and see which is closer to most of the ages.
The mean is $38.2$ and the median is $32$, so the median (choice B) is the better summary.

explanation: Add the five ages and divide by $5$ to get the mean: $(30 + 31 + 32 + 33 + 65) \div 5 = 191 \div 5 = 38.2$.
The median is the middle of the ordered ages $30, 31, 32, 33, 65$, which is $32$.
The outlier $65$ pulls the mean up to $38.2$, which is older than four of the five teachers.
The median $32$ is close to most of the ages, so the median, choice B, is the better summary.
